<<top_bar>>
The ferry at Low Harbor – A debt of nine crowns – The
cartographer hires a boy – Salt on the wind.
<<bottom_bar>>

The ferry came into Low Harbor on the last tide of
October, 1871, riding so low that the gulls walked its
rail like inspectors. Ada Quill stepped off with a brass
theodolite in one hand and a letter of credit in the
other, and neither was worth what she had been promised.

The harbormaster was a narrow man named Osric Penn who
kept his ledgers in a biscuit tin. He told her the
survey office had closed in the spring and that the nine
crowns owed to her were owed, in turn, by a man who had
drowned. She thanked him. It was, she said, the most
complete account of a debt she had ever received.
